<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e22315238f9426708e10cfff1d6a96e56cca33a1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

git fetch origin e22315238f9426708e10cfff1d6a96e56cca33a1 05acc5d51fe577358bbdbb714f08983e2c7d1647 && git checkout -B drift-repro e22315238f9426708e10cfff1d6a96e56cca33a1 && git merge --no-ff 05acc5d51fe577358bbdbb714f08983e2c7d1647

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `05acc5d51fe577358bbdbb714f08983e2c7d1647`
Local-runs: none

Rendered 2026-10-10T06:33Z on PR #22625 (card #22607). The head is the merge of `origin/main` `18d999031b` into the branch; the merge-base against `origin/main` `e22315238f` is `18d999031b`, so the net diff is 7 files, +383 / -15. Inputs: the card body and its three comments (triage `6093976698`, claim `6094034487`, `os-dev-report` `6094566317`), the PR body and file list, the net diff `origin/main...05acc5d51f`, and the head's check-runs. Read-only: nothing was built, run or re-run; every derived gate family is answered by the check-runs below.

**Check-runs on the head** (latest run per name; read six times, one curl a minute, until none was in progress; the last run completed 2026-10-10T06:31Z): 35 runs, 33 `success`, 2 `skipped` (`Console Pin Gate`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 failed, 0 still running. All seven required contexts green: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (the aggregate and all 6 shards), `Dogfood Regression Gate` (the aggregate and all 3 shards), `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Spec property liveness`, the four claim and closing-target gates and the four `Type Check ·` gates are green too.

### ① Derived judgments

Governance frame first: the file list touches no governed surface (no `docs/adr/**`, `.claude/**`, `skills/**`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`); head repo equals base repo; 398 changed lines. This record is owed because the claim declares `Clause-②: yes`, not because of a path hit.

1. **Accept-set: unchanged — right.** No `packages/spec` file moves; `ApprovalNodeConfig` and `ApproverType` are untouched; `openNodeRequest`'s input type and return type are byte-identical to `main`; no REST route is added or widened, so no closed query-parameter set is owed. `check:api-surface`, `check:authorable-surface` and the liveness gate are green on the head, which agrees.

2. **Public surface: one new notification topic, `approval.requested`, emitted by `openNodeRequest` — right, and placed right.** It goes through the private `notify()` ingress (ADR-0030 single ingress) in the same call shape as `approval.reminder` and `approval.reassigned`: `audience` of one approver, `actorContext: context`, `source: sys_approval_request`, a per-approver `dedupKey`, and `actionUrl: '/system/approvals'` which `notify()` rewrites centrally to `?request=ID`. No second path, no direct inbox write. Measured at the head: `this.notify({` has 13 call sites (12 on `main`), and the body battery's "twelve of the thirteen" count matches. The topic is declared nowhere else: `approval.reminder` occurs outside `plugin-approvals` only in the changeset and the QA checklist, so no catalog, i18n bundle or preference list is owed; ADR-0012 line 143 already names `approval.requested` as its Layer-1 example, so the name is on record. The dev's hypothesis (1) — no spec stop — is confirmed on the head tree.

3. **Recipient rule — right, and it is the reminder's.** `openedOn` is the slate the request actually opened on (after OOO delegation and after an `onEmptyApprovers: 'fallback'` replacement), filtered by the same concrete-identity predicate `remind()` uses (`!a.includes(':')`), de-duplicated by `Set`, minus OOO delegates already told by `approval.ooo_substituted`. Consequences I checked against the source: `admin_rescue` opens on literals only, so zero emits; `auto_approve` returns before any write, zero; `fail` throws before any write, zero; `fallback` tells the fallback approvers. The fan-out is the last statement before `return`, after `mirrorStatusField`, so a half-opened request tells no one. A failing channel is caught inside `notify()` and logged at `warn` with the topic — a functional degradation, correctly below `error`.

4. **Actor forwarding — right.** `actorContext: context` hands the ExecutionContext, never a string; `recordedActor()` yields the person or nothing (ADR-0118 D1); the widened actor battery pins `u_sub` on the `link`-opened request and the machine-actor case stays in that file's existing pin.

5. **Pins cover triage's three.** (a) one message per resolved approver — new file test 1 (a named user plus two position holders give exactly three single-audience emits in the reminder's payload shape, with deep link and actor), tests 2 and 3 (a twice-listed person told once; a literal slot tells nobody); (b) the empty-slate control with `onEmptyApprovers` deciding — four cases, `fallback` as the positive arm; (c) ablation — reported 12 red / 359 green with the fan-out loop emptied and a trap-proved restore. The arithmetic agrees with the diff: 6 positive pins in the new file + 2 widened batteries + 4 scoped `approval-service.test.ts` assertions = 12, and the 3 no-emit controls stay green by construction. Real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver`, no new fake engine. The four `approval-service.test.ts` edits splice the opening's emit off and keep their original assertions unchanged — right.

6. **Docs — right on every sentence I could check.** The `approvals.mdx` callout is rewritten from "notifies nobody" to the new rule, naming who is told, who is not and why, and the double-notify remedy. `:380`, plus the bounded in-place fixes at `:32` and the `manager` callout, name **Setup → Users → ⋯ → Set Manager** — verified at the head: `sys_user` declares the `set_user_manager` row action labelled "Set Manager" targeting `POST /api/v1/auth/admin/set-user-manager` (`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-user.object.ts:372`–`:378`). #22584's sentence (`:384`–`:386`) is untouched and the single-writer-path gate is green. "Without a messaging service, no approval notification is delivered at all" is true: `notify()` returns 0 on a missing messaging surface. No other hand-written page states the old rule: a head-wide grep for "notifies nobody", "approval.opened" and "Opening a request notif" hits only the QA checklist (③).

7. **Workaround census — accepted as reported, and the verdict does not rest on it.** The in-repo half (8 approval flows, 15 nodes, one `notify` node and it runs after the decision) is consistent with `examples/app-showcase` at the head; the hotcrm and hotclm halves are the dev's readings at named commits and lie outside this record's inputs. The changeset names the remedy for out-of-tree apps regardless.

8. **Hygiene.** `[#22607]` in a code comment follows the file's existing convention (56 such anchors on `main`); no tracker number in a runtime string; no model identifier in the diff; no release-owned or auto-generated file touched; the PR footer is the session-URL form.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22607-approval-opened-topic.md` declares `"@objectstack/plugin-approvals": minor` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — one arm from the closed pair, matching the PR body's `Clause-②: yes`. Right: `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` is a released package (17.7.0, not private); the diff adds behaviour (a new topic, new inbox rows per opening) and removes or renames nothing an author can write, so `minor` is the floor and `patch` would be wrong; nothing is breaking, so no ADR-0087 disposition marker is owed and `skip-changeset` would be wrong. The body states what is new, who is told, who is not, what is not included (one-tap links), and the one migration-shaped note a consumer needs (remove a `notify` node that only told the approvers at opening). `Check Changeset` is green.

Clause-②: yes (widening) — a new public notification topic on a released package; the changeset declares it; nothing in the diff narrows.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **ADR-0043 `:40`–`:42`, "(Open-time notification remains the flow author's `notify` node; templates there can adopt the same links later.)" — answered: a v1 scope note, not a recorded decision; the PR reverses nothing in ADR-0043 and leaves one parenthetical stale.** I read the ADR at the head. Its decision is the seven-row token table (scope, storage, single-use, TTL, identity, invalidation, scanner-proof) and the mechanics that enforce it; the parenthetical qualifies the "Issue" bullet's wiring ("Wired into `remind()`"), says "remains" (status quo) and "later" (anticipates change), weighs no alternative, gives no rationale, and open-time notification is not among its "Non-goals (v1)". Everything the ADR decides still holds after this PR: tokens are minted in `remind()` only and the opening carries none. ADR-0030's single-ingress decision names "approval requests" as a producer and ADR-0012 names `approval.requested`, so the ADR record as a whole points where this PR goes. Prime Directive 13 is not breached, and keeping `docs/adr/**` out of this PR was right (Tier H). **Escalated to the maintainer, option A:** a one-line status amendment on ADR-0043 in a docs-only Tier H PR, saying open-time notification is now the service's `approval.requested` topic and one-tap links remain `remind()`-only. The same PR should touch `skills/objectstack-automation/references/state-machines-and-approvals.md:382`–`:383` ("rather than expecting the node to send mail itself"), which I found stale in the same way and which is `skills/**`, Tier H too. Not a FAIL ground.

2. **One-tap Approve / Reject links on the opening — answered: no, option A as shipped.** ADR-0043 scopes token minting to `remind()` by its own text; minting two 72-hour bearer tokens per approver on every opening widens the session-less bypass lane the ADR calls "deliberate, narrow", and that is an ADR amendment, not a card rider. The card asks that approvers be told, and the opening message deep-links to the request. The changeset and the guide both say the links are reminder-only, so no reader is misled. Not escalated; a future demand goes through an ADR-0043 amendment first.

3. **`docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/approvals.json` `:341` (`knownGaps`: "opening a request notifies NOBODY … there is no approval.opened topic") and `:394` (`source`: "the emitting topic set, which has no approval.opened member") — answered: stale after this PR, harmless, correctly outside the claim surface; escalated for a carrier.** `:400` is a dated `history` row and stays true as history. The fixtures still drive `remind` and `reassign`, so no checklist run misreads, and `check:platform-checklist` rides the green `Lint & Repo Gates`. The dev named no carrier. **Escalated to the dispatching seat:** file a small docs-only follow-up card on the checklist, or fold it into the next `checklist-author` sweep, so the `knownGaps` note is removed and the `source` note names `approval.requested`. Not a FAIL ground.

4. No other dev flag. The report's `premise_still_valid: true` holds on the head: `main` at `18d999031b` had no opening topic before this diff. The two serial constraints the claim cleared are honoured: #22589's files (`request-read-gate.ts`, `approvals-plugin.ts`) are untouched here, and #22584's sentence (`approvals.mdx:384`–`:386`) is unchanged — the same-page hunk edits `:380`–`:381` only.
